headline: OpenAI reopens Pro $200 subscriptions with usage changes, effectively halving API cost
summary: OpenAI is re-opening its $200 Pro subscriptions to new users tomorrow. The plan includes revised usage calculations, effectively halving the API spend compared to the previous Pro $200 plan.
details: OpenAI is set to re-open its $200 Pro subscriptions for new users starting tomorrow. This re-introduction comes with a significant change to how usage is calculated, effectively cutting the API spend in half compared to the previous iteration of the Pro $200 plan.

The company stated that while the subscription fee remains $200, the underlying usage metrics have been adjusted. This change aims to provide more value to subscribers, allowing for greater API utilization for the same cost.

headline_marked: [[Opera for Android integrates eSIM]] with 3GB free data, solving travel connectivity issues
headline: Opera for Android integrates eSIM with 3GB free data, solving travel connectivity issues
summary: Opera for Android now allows users to buy travel eSIMs directly from the browser, offering 3GB of free data with a three-day validity for 47 destinations. This eliminates the need for airport lines and paperwork when traveling internationally.
details: Opera for Android is the first browser to integrate an eSIM, allowing users to purchase travel eSIMs directly from within the app. It offers a free trial with 3GB of data valid for three days, which can be claimed without any purchase.

This feature aims to simplify international travel by letting users set up mobile connectivity from home, avoiding airport queues and paperwork. The free data package is exclusive to Opera for Android phones running Android 10 or newer.

The eSIM activation is flexible; the plan's validity period only begins upon connecting to a network in the destination country. Users must, however, activate the eSIM within a year of claiming the offer.

The service supports 47 destinations worldwide, including most European countries, the US, UK, and several Asian nations like South Korea and Thailand. Users can also top up the same eSIM for multiple countries within a single trip.
To utilize this feature, the Android phone must support eSIM functionality and be carrier-unlocked. This ensures compatibility and seamless integration with the new browser-based service.
